newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore man fined $43,000 for Internet smut.
newsitem.headline: Singapore man fined $43,000 for Internet smut.

text.p: A Singapore man has been fined Singapore $61,000 (US$43,000) for downloading sex films from the Internet, the first such case in a country embarking on censoring the net, the Straits Times said on Wednesday.
The newspaper said Lai Chee Chuan, 41, was fined S$1,000 each for 61 obscene films he said he had downloaded from the Internet for his own use.
He was also fined S$500 for possessing a magazine -- Penthouse, deemed obscene in Singapore -- found by police when they raided Lai's flat.

The newspaper quoted police as saying the raid followed a tip-off from Interpol that it was investigating a group of people exchanging pornography on the Internet and a Singapore site had been identified.
It said other sites were in South Africa, Hong Kong, Britain, Canada and Germany, but gave no further details.
The newspaper did not say whether Lai's computer was one of the sites.
Singapore has been regulating access to the Internet since September 15 by obliging access providers to install special "proxy" computers which can be used to block specific sites.

Officials say that so far only a few dozen, high-profile sites have been blocked in Singapore's battle against what it calls pornography and political views it says could be dangerous in this multi-racial society.
